userMessages.text:
# Multi-region commerce failover

We operate a customer-facing commerce API in three regions. Global DNS and an anycast edge route users to the nearest healthy regional ingress. Each region has a web application, API gateway, identity cache, catalog service, cart service, checkout service, order service, worker pool, event bus, Redis cluster, and an independent observability collector spread across multiple availability zones. Regional service discovery and circuit breakers keep a failing instance or zone from taking down the region.

Catalog reads come from a globally replicated document store and may continue from a local replica during inter-region isolation. Cart data uses a multi-region key-value store with per-cart ownership and conditional writes so concurrent updates are detected. Checkout creates orders in a single writable home region selected for each customer. The home region commits an order and its outbox event atomically to its regional relational database, then streams database changes to warm replicas in the other two regions. Payment requests go through a global payment adapter that assigns an idempotency key before calling either of two external payment providers.

A global control plane receives health signals from synthetic probes, regional collectors, database replication monitors, and event-bus lag monitors. It distinguishes an instance failure, availability-zone failure, regional service failure, database write failure, and full regional isolation. The control plane can remove a region from new traffic automatically, but promoting a relational replica to writer requires a failover lease from the quorum store and confirmation that replication lag is within the recovery-point objective. Only one region may hold the writer lease. DNS and edge routing change after promotion, and the order coordinator resumes from the promoted outbox without issuing duplicate payments.

During a full home-region loss, existing carts remain available from the global store, catalog stays readable, and checkout pauses until the writer lease moves. Requests already carrying an order id may be retried safely. Events crossing regions use a replication bridge with deduplication, quarantine for schema incompatibility, and replay controls. A dead-letter service retains exhausted worker messages in each region and copies their metadata to the operations account.

Configuration, feature flags, signing keys, and service identities originate in the control plane but are cached regionally with explicit expiry behavior. Expired identity material stops privileged writes while allowing public health checks. Audit events from routing changes, lease decisions, database promotion, provider failover, replay, and operator overrides enter an immutable global audit store. Paging, incident records, and the status service receive the same failover milestones.

Recovery must cover failback as well as failover. The recovered region rejoins first as a read replica, catches up, validates checksums and event offsets, and receives shadow traffic before it can serve users. Returning writer ownership is a separate controlled operation; it is never implied merely because the original region is healthy again. Capacity safeguards prevent the two surviving regions from accepting more traffic than their tested limits, and load shedding protects checkout and order recovery ahead of catalog personalization.
